data.current_description: Returns the slice of the model catalog that is currently routable. The Router is generally available: every organization may route to any catalog model, so the listing is shaped by routability, not by per-organization enrollment. The catalog digest identifies the release-pinned catalog that produced the listing so support can correlate a caller's view with an exact release. The listing is advisory: admission remains the enforcement point for access gates and credit. By default the response includes every public model. The optional language, objective, and path parameters select the exact benchmark projection used to order and annotate the rows.
data.summary_suggestion: Discover available routable models with optional filtering
data.description_suggestion: Returns the currently routable models from the catalog. The listing reflects routability across all organizations, not per-organization enrollment. Includes a catalog digest for release correlation. The response is advisory; actual admission enforcement occurs at request time. By default returns all public models. Optional parameters: language (filter by language), objective (filter by routing objective), and path (select benchmark projection for ordering and annotation). Use this to discover which models are available before routing requests.

data.current_description: For live audio, open the streaming socket at /v1/stt/stream, specified in asyncapi.yaml. This operation is the batch path, for a recording that already exists. The audio always travels as an uploaded part, never as a URL: the Router fetches nothing on a caller's behalf. For idempotency the content hash covers the decoded part payload bytes only — no part headers, no boundary bytes — concatenated in part order (request, then audio), so a retry hashes identically no matter what boundary string the client generates. Usage lives in the response body; there is deliberately no STT usage header.
data.description_suggestion: Transcribes a pre-recorded audio file provided as a multipart upload. This is the batch operation; for live streaming audio, use /v1/stt/stream (WebSocket). Audio must be uploaded as a part, not referenced by URL. Supports idempotent retries via content hash of decoded audio bytes (excluding headers and boundaries). Returns a transcription response with usage metrics in the body (not in headers). Specify audio format and language via request parameters.

data.current_summary: Synthesize one utterance to a raw audio stream
data.current_description: For speech that starts playing before the text is finished, open the streaming socket at /v1/tts/stream, specified in asyncapi.yaml. This operation is the one-shot path, synthesizing a single utterance in full. The response body is a raw audio stream in the requested output format; the route and the billed character count come back in headers (Speko-Provider, Speko-Model, Speko-Region, Speko-Usage-Characters) because a byte stream has no place for a JSON envelope.
data.description_suggestion: Synthesizes text to speech, returning a complete raw audio stream in the requested format. This is the one-shot operation; for streaming synthesis where audio plays before text finishes, use /v1/tts/stream (WebSocket). Accepts text input and audio format specification. Returns raw audio bytes in the response body; routing details and character usage are provided in response headers (Speko-Provider, Speko-Model, Speko-Region, Speko-Usage-Characters). Specify voice, language, and output format via request parameters.

data.current_summary: Generate an LLM response, as JSON or as a server-sent event stream
data.current_description: Generates a response for the supplied conversation history. With stream omitted or false the body is a single application/json LLMResponse; with stream true the body is a text/event-stream whose event payloads are documented by the ResponseCreated, ResponseItemAdded, ResponseTextDelta, ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDelta, ResponseItemCompleted, ResponseCompleted, and ErrorEnvelope schemas. Response ids are Speko-minted (resp_<request-id>); provider response and conversation ids never appear in output — they are captured only as content-free telemetry evidence. There is no previous_response_id anywhere in the contract: callers resend full history, including function results, on every request.
data.description_suggestion: Generates an LLM response for the provided conversation history. Supports two output modes: non-streaming (stream=false, default) returns a complete LLMResponse as JSON; streaming (stream=true) returns server-sent events with deltas (ResponseCreated, ResponseItemAdded, ResponseTextDelta, ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDelta, ResponseItemCompleted, ResponseCompleted). Response IDs are Speko-generated (resp_<request-id>). Requires full conversation history on each request, including any prior function results; there is no previous_response_id field. Provider IDs and conversation IDs are not exposed in responses. Supports function calling and structured output via request configuration.

data.current_summary: Evaluate typed questions against shared state with Jev
data.current_description: Executes one non-streaming TypeSafe Jev evaluation. Routing must be explicit. The Router preserves native question ids, option keys, probabilities, confidence, Score legends, and reported usage. The application owns every decision and subsequent action.
data.summary_suggestion: Execute a TypeSafe Jev evaluation with explicit routing
data.description_suggestion: Executes a non-streaming TypeSafe Jev evaluation to score or rank options against typed questions. Requires explicit routing configuration (auto-routing is not supported). Input: typed questions, options, and shared evaluation state. Output: preserves native question IDs, option keys, probabilities, confidence scores, Score legends, and usage metrics. The application is responsible for interpreting results and making downstream decisions. Use this for deterministic, schema-validated evaluations where you need full control over provider selection.
